soak-5.note: Scenario on M1b: 5 clusters, one window, the Pods table of wh-perf-01, a follow of the chatter pod (10 lines/s) and a periodic visit to ConfigMaps (2,000 rows), Deployments and Pods. Measured after the review fixes (the clients now really connect to the test cluster), as a 30-minute run: the 60-minute run of the design was shortened. footprintGrowthMB is minute 10 to the last minute. The footprint moves in steps of 15-20 MB with the navigation cycle (the ConfigMaps store is built and released), so a short run can land on either phase: a 15-minute run of the same build measured +19 MB (minute 10 on a low step, the last minute on a high one; lows 135 MB at minutes 6, 10 and 12, leaks 0), the 30-minute run -9 MB. cpuAvgPct is high because a visible log follow re-renders the SwiftUI log screen several times a second (a P1 item); soak budgets are memory growth, leaks, threads and file descriptors.

terminalScrollbackCost.note: about 5.4 MB per full 5,000-line terminal at 120 columns, below the 12 MB estimate of section 12.3.2

note: M1b: the Mac shell with the shared iOS screens, KubeTable, the log table, the YAML editor and SwiftTerm. Sampler numbers come from scripts/perf-sample.sh on a Profile build against the test cluster (perf contexts, namespace wh-perf with 80 pods: the single-node test cluster cannot schedule 100). Warnings against M1a are expected: M1a was an empty placeholder window.

environment.machine: Apple silicon Mac (not the MacBook Air M1 reference Mac)
environment.power: on power, caffeinate -disu during the soak
